claim: The scientific method involves forming hypotheses designing experiments collecting data and drawing conclusions through systematic observation
Falsifiability proposed by Karl Popper requires that scientific theories must be capable of being proven wrong through observation
The is-ought problem identified by David Hume states that descriptive facts about the world cannot logically justify normative ethical claims
Utilitarianism evaluates the morality of actions based on their consequences seeking to maximize overall wellbeing or happiness
Deontological ethics judges actions by whether they conform to moral rules or duties regardless of their consequences
Virtue ethics focuses on the character of the moral agent rather than rules or consequences emphasizing practical wisdom
The mind-body problem asks how mental states relate to physical brain states and whether consciousness can be reduced to neural activity
Phenomenology studies the structures of conscious experience as lived and experienced from the first-person perspective
Existentialism emphasizes individual freedom responsibility and the search for meaning in a universe without inherent purpose
The Socratic method uses guided questioning to stimulate critical thinking and illuminate ideas through dialogue
Occam razor recommends preferring the simplest explanation among competing hypotheses that equally account for the evidence
Thomas Kuhn argued that science progresses through paradigm shifts where established frameworks are replaced by fundamentally new ones
The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis proposes that the structure of a language influences how its speakers perceive and think about the world
Critical thinking involves analyzing evaluating and constructing arguments using evidence logic and reasoning rather than appeals to authority
The precautionary principle holds that the burden of proof for potentially harmful actions falls on those proposing the action
Information asymmetry occurs when one party in a transaction has more relevant knowledge than the other creating potential for exploitation
The tragedy of the anticommons occurs when too many parties hold rights of exclusion preventing efficient use of a resource
Ubuntu is an African philosophical concept meaning I am because we are emphasizing communal bonds and shared humanity
Epistemic humility is the recognition that our knowledge is always incomplete and our beliefs may be wrong
The veil of ignorance thought experiment asks what principles of justice people would choose if they did not know their own position in society
